reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to assess whether the adoptive T-cell therapy engaged melanoma antigens. The trial was terminated early due to withdrawal of CRADA partner with only 3 patients enrolled. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to confirm T-cell activation or cytotoxicity. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (clinical response by RECIST) was not met. Only 1 of 3 patients achieved partial response (33%), with 2 having progressive disease. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: With only 3 patients, no meaningful subgroup analysis possible. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Major confounders include severely underpowered study (N=3), early termination for non-scientific reasons (CRADA partner withdrawal), and insufficient sample size to draw meaningful conclusions about efficacy.

failure_modes.evidence: Only 3 patients enrolled before early termination due to CRADA partner withdrawal. Sample size far too small to assess efficacy of adoptive T-cell therapy.
Study was terminated due to withdrawal of CRADA partner, not for scientific or safety reasons.
